To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have implemented an 8 bit fixed point dynamic convolutional neural network topology, which has been trained for human sign language recognition, and we have obtained an accuracy of 79.7\ and a frame rate 6.4 fps with a clock frequency 250 MHz.
we have implemented an FPGA based accelerator for the inference of a Convolutional Neural Networks for Human Sign Language recognition.

- A 8 bit dynamic point fixed point implementation of the ZynqNet convolutional neural network has been successfully implemented on a Xilinx Zynq FPGA board and it is capable of recognising human hand gestures from a video stream.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the implementation of a neural network on an embedded FPGA board, and the main contribution is the successful adaptation of the ZynqNet topology to a new task, i. e. human sign language recognition, and the implementation of the convolutional layers on an FPGA device.
the implementation and optimisation of a Convolutional Neural network on an FPGA platform for the recognition of hand gestures.
the design of a convolutional neural networks accelerator for the recognition of human sign language gestures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the implementation of Zynqnet on an FPGA board has been successfully carried out and it has been tested with the dataset of hand signs.
the hardware implementation of the ZynqNet convolutional neural network has been successfully accomplished and that the accuracy achieved in the test set is promising.
this work has successfully demonstrated the feasibility of the implementation of a convolutional neural net work on an FPGA device and its potential for human sign language recognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have successfully implemented an 8 bit fixed point dynamic neural network topology on a Xilinx Zynq 7045 FPGA platform, and we have trained it for the task of human sign language recognition, obtaining an accuracy of 81\% for the inference tests and a frame rate 6.4 fps.
we have been able to successfully implement a convolutional network topology, which has been trained with ImageNet, on a Zynq FPGA platform, for the task of recognising hand signs.

the implementation of the convolutional layer on an FPGA device is feasible and the results achieved show that it is a good candidate to be used as a hardware accelerator for image classification tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it has been demonstrated that a convolutional neural net can be implemented on an FPGA device and it can be trained with a different task, in our case the human sign language recognition task, than the one it was initially proposed for, i.e. the image recognition task.
it is possible to implement a convolution neural network on FPGA with an accuracy that is competitive with other state of the art solutions.
the hardware implementation of ZynqNet is feasible and it can achieve an accuracy of 79\ with a frame rate of more than 5 FPS on an FPGA platform.
